llm_qa_history.system_prompt:
You are a top-tier scientist with deep expertise across physics, biology,
chemistry, and materials science. Your task is to act as a "Novelty Evaluator":
objectively judge whether a newly generated mathematical equation is
"scientifically novel" within its given scientific context.

CORE CRITERIA:
- NOT NOVEL: the equation is a well-known classical formula that already exists
  in textbooks, on the internet, or in the open scientific literature — i.e. a
  formula that could be obtained simply by recall/recitation.
- NOVEL: while remaining scientifically sound, the equation introduces uncommon,
  nonlinear, or genuinely new composite mechanism terms, such that neither a
  human nor an AI could guess it from background knowledge alone — it could only
  be recovered through data-driven inference from experimental observations.

[SCIENTIFIC CONTEXT]:
Field: biology
Problem description: A seasonally forced infection shows recurrent yearly waves driven by periodic variation in transmissibility tied to environmental cycles. Epidemiologists observe repeated epidemic peaks in the infectious population that neither die out nor grow without bound. The periodic modulation of transmission combined with recovery and susceptible replenishment sustains the oscillations. The amplitude and period of environmental forcing are fixed inputs to the dynamics.

[VARIABLES & PARAMETERS]:
- Target variable: dI_dt (Rate of change of the infectious fraction under seasonal forcing)
- Input features: t (time)
- Dynamic states: S (Fraction of the population that is susceptible); I (Fraction of the population that is infectious); R (Fraction of the population that is recovered/immune but subject to waning); C (Mobilized public-health/care response capacity acting to remove infectious individuals)
- Parameters: beta0 (Baseline transmission rate); eps (Amplitude of seasonal forcing in transmission); T_period (Period of environmental forcing); gamma (Recovery rate); mu (Per-capita birth/death (turnover) rate); pi (Mathematical constant pi); gamma_sat (Maximum additional per-capita removal rate from saturating care capacity); I_half (Infectious fraction at which additional removal reaches half its maximum); rho (Per-capita rate at which recovered individuals lose immunity and become reactivatable); I_waning (Infectious fraction above which crowding suppresses relapse-driven reactivation); omega (Baseline rate of loss of immunity feeding recovered individuals back toward susceptibility); kappa (Per-capita removal efficacy of mobilized response capacity acting on the infectious pool); c_prod (Rate at which response capacity is mobilized in proportion to current infection burden); c_decay (Relaxation/decay rate of mobilized response capacity when infection subsides); C_sat (Saturation level limiting how much response capacity can be mobilized); delta_syn (Maximum fractional synergistic boost to removal efficacy when response capacity is highly mobilized); C_half (Response capacity level at which the synergistic efficacy boost reaches half its maximum)

[CANDIDATE EQUATION]:
dI_dt = beta0*(1 + eps*cos(2*pi*t/T_period))*S*I - (gamma + mu)*I - gamma_sat*I**2/(I_half + I) + gamma*rho*R*exp(-I/I_waning) - kappa*C*I - kappa*C*I*(delta_syn*C/(C_half + C))

[CLOSED ODE SYSTEM]:
{
  "time_symbol": "t",
  "target_state": "I",
  "states": [
    {
      "symbol": "S",
      "rhs": "mu - beta0*(1 + eps*cos(2*pi*t/T_period))*S*I - mu*S + omega*R",
      "initial_condition": 0.6,
      "description": "Fraction of the population that is susceptible"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "I",
      "rhs": "beta0*(1 + eps*cos(2*pi*t/T_period))*S*I - (gamma + mu)*I - gamma_sat*I**2/(I_half + I) + gamma*rho*R*exp(-I/I_waning) - kappa*C*I - kappa*C*I*(delta_syn*C/(C_half + C))",
      "initial_condition": 0.01,
      "description": "Fraction of the population that is infectious"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "R",
      "rhs": "gamma*I - mu*R - omega*R - gamma*rho*R*exp(-I/I_waning)",
      "initial_condition": 0.39,
      "description": "Fraction of the population that is recovered/immune and subject to waning"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "C",
      "rhs": "c_prod*I*(1 - C/C_sat) - c_decay*C",
      "initial_condition": 0.0,
      "description": "Mobilized public-health/care response capacity that builds with infection burden and relaxes when infection subsides"
    }
  ]
}
(Note: this equation comes from an equation-evolution pipeline; assume it is
mathematically solvable and numerically stable.)

[NOTE ON KNOWN / CLASSICAL TERMS]:
The classical / textbook starting point for this phenomenon (the baseline equation) is:
  dI_dt = beta0*(1 + eps*cos(2*pi*t/T_period))*S*I - (gamma + mu)*I
The terms appearing in this baseline equation can be regarded as the well-known classical terms for this problem. 3. Assess whether it has true novelty (i.e. it could only be discovered by

Provide your final answer STRICTLY in the following JSON format, with no extra
